record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one use Riemann–Hilbert and nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof of the asymptotic binary-periodic behavior claimed for the Toda shock problem with exponential forces and supercritical drive?

evidence.quote: The first is to use Riemann–Hilbert/steepest-descent methods to prove the results in Venakides et al. rigorously.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the doubly infinite Toda lattice
\[
\ddot q_n(t) = e^{q_{n-1}(t)-q_n(t)} - e^{q_n(t)-q_{n+1}(t)}, \qquad n\in\mathbb Z,\; t\ge 0,
\]
with the "Toda shock" initial-boundary data driven by a supercritical exponential forcing on one side: assume that for some constants $a>0$ (the drive strength, taken in the supercritical regime where standard linear shock solutions fail to exist) and appropriate decay on the other side, the data and forcing produce a propagating shock front. Formal modulation/Whitham analysis predicts that, for large $t$, the lattice variables $q_n(t)$ are asymptotically described, in the shock region $n/t$ inside an interval $(c_-,c_+)$, by a binary-periodic (two-band, period-two in $n$) traveling profile whose modulation parameters depend on the rescaled space-time variable $\xi=n/t$.

Problem: Using the inverse scattering transform together with the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest-descent method applied to the associated $2\times 2$ matrix Riemann–Hilbert factorization problem for the Toda lattice with step-like / exponentially forced boundary conditions, give a fully rigorous proof that the long-time asymptotic behavior of $q_n(t)$ in the shock region is given by the conjectured binary-periodic (modulated two-band) formula, with explicit error estimates uniform on compact subsets of $\xi\in(c_-,c_+)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A program of Egorova, Michor, Teschl and collaborators has, using Riemann–Hilbert / nonlinear steepest-descent techniques, rigorously justified the long-time asymptotics of the classical Toda shock wave with step-like constant backgrounds in all principal regions of the space-time half-plane, including the modulated finite-gap (two-band) middle region, verifying the Venakides–Deift–Oba conjecture in those settings. The specific variant with exponential forcing in the supercritical drive regime does not appear to have a published fully rigorous Riemann–Hilbert proof; the standard step-like Toda shock case is solved, so the broader problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Long-time asymptotics for Toda shock waves in the modulation region
status_evidence.snippet: Toda shock waves are asymptotically close to a modulated finite gap solution in the region separating the soliton and the elliptic wave regions.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous Riemann–Hilbert asymptotics for the Toda shock in the modulation region, verifying the two-band modulated description.

status_evidence.title: How Discrete Spectrum and Resonances Influence the Asymptotics of the Toda Shock Wave
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorously derived the long-time asymptotics of the Toda shock wave in the middle region where the solution is asymptotically finite gap.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous justification of finite-gap (binary-periodic-type) asymptotics for the standard Toda shock.

status_evidence.title: Long-time asymptotics for the Toda shock problem: non-overlapping spectra
status_evidence.snippet: Formulas for the leading terms of the long-time asymptotics for the Toda shock wave were derived by the method of nonlinear steepest descent in all principal domains.
status_evidence.claim: Nonlinear steepest descent rigorously applied to the Toda shock problem.
